properties.name: Philadelphia to Cumberland Valley
properties.description: The first inland movement from Philadelphia. Ulster Scots settled in Cumberland Valley (Lancaster, York, Cumberland counties), establishing the base for further southward migration.

properties.name: The Great Wagon Road: Pennsylvania to Virginia
properties.description: The Great Wagon Road became the primary migration route for Scotch-Irish families. This section runs through Maryland into Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, a fertile region between the Blue Ridge and Allegheny Mountains.

properties.name: Shenandoah Valley to Western North Carolina
properties.description: Continuing south along the Great Wagon Road through the Blue Ridge piedmont into western North Carolina. The Yadkin River valley became a major Scotch-Irish settlement area.

properties.name: Western North Carolina to South Carolina Backcountry
properties.description: The Great Wagon Road's southern terminus in South Carolina's backcountry (Piedmont region). Scotch-Irish settlers established Presbyterian communities throughout the upcountry.

properties.name: Cumberland Gap to Kentucky
properties.description: After the Revolutionary War, settlers poured through the Cumberland Gap into Kentucky. Daniel Boone blazed the Wilderness Road in 1775. McCreary families were among the early Kentucky pioneers.

properties.name: Virginia to Tennessee
properties.description: Scotch-Irish families moved into what would become Tennessee, following river valleys through the mountains. The Watauga and Holston settlements became major Scotch-Irish centers.
